jobs.title: Tenure Track Faculty in Sustainable Tourism and Hospitality
jobs.description:
**Position Summary:**

**Job Description:**

Western Colorado University invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track position in Sustainable Tourism and Hospitality. We seek a dynamic teacher-scholar who is committed to student-centered learning, professional preparation, and inclusive, interdisciplinary education. This is an in-person, on-campus position on our vibrant residential campus in Gunnison, Colorado.

Located in the heart of Colorado’s world-renowned tourism and outdoor recreation region, Western offers students a one-of-a-kind environment to learn, lead, and grow. Surrounded by top ski resorts, national parks, boutique lodges, and adventure tourism hubs, students gain direct access to the very settings where hospitality excellence is both expected and tested — and these same lessons apply on a global scale. Students gain expertise in key areas such as marketing, human resources, real estate, finance, data analytics, and facilities management.

The standard teaching load is 24 credit hours per academic year. The successful candidate will deliver engaging, well-designed courses in tourism and hospitality, including an introductory course, Resort Operations and Management, as well as other courses aligned with their expertise and departmental needs. The successful candidate will also work with faculty in the Business School to reimagine this program toward experience management (including sports, entertainment, and more). We especially value faculty who engage students in high-impact practices such as internships, research, community-based learning, and who participate in our Western Watershed General Education and First-Year Seminar Headwaters courses. We prepare students for a livelihood based on their values and aid students in gaining post-graduate opportunities.

The School of Business serves over 325 students across its majors and minors. Students can earn a degree in Business Administration and Economics, with emphases in energy management, finance, management, and marketing, combining rigorous academic preparation with high-impact experiential learning.

Western supports its faculty by fostering a collaborative and innovative academic community. Our Teaching and Learning Center (TLC) actively engages faculty, staff, and administrators in cross-campus initiatives designed to reimagine WCU’s educational landscape—rooted in diverse expertise and committed to continuous growth. The Professional Activity Fund (PAF) provides financial support for faculty engaged in research, artistic projects, grant writing, and other scholarly or creative activities, with three application opportunities each year.

Western’s faculty are teacher-scholars who contribute meaningfully to their discipline, the campus, our community, and beyond. We seek candidates who will actively support our institutional mission and strategic priorities, including:

  

* Participating in our innovative Western Watershed General Education program
* Promoting wellness, inclusion, and belonging
* Collaborating within and across disciplines to grow enrollment and deepen student engagement
* Expanding career-connected learning and professional pathways

Learn more about the department at: https://western.edu/department/school-of-business/

**QUALIFICATIONS:** A Ph.D. or similar degree in the tourism and/or hospitality areas or related field is required. ABD considered for hire, completed degree required for tenure. Candidates must have a demonstrated commitment to undergraduate education, excellence in teaching, and willingness to work with and be sensitive to the educational needs of all students. Also required is the ability for research and professional development within a related field of study, and experience in university service. Candidates must also be able to use technology in instructional delivery, including the ability to teach online and hybrid courses. Collegiality and professional flexibility are sought in the successful candidate.

**SALARY/BENEFITS:** The annualized salary range for this position depends on incoming rank (assistant professor or associate professor), qualifications, and experience.

  

* Assistant Professor - $90,000 to $100,000
* Associate Professor - $100,000 to $110,000

Western offers an excellent benefits package, including shared premiums for comprehensive health insurance, dental insurance, retirement benefits, life insurance, and additional insurance options. After one year of employment, Western provides free tuition for eligible dependents enrolled full-time in undergraduate programs for up to four years.

**START DATE:** January 6, 2027 or August 16, 2027

**APPLICATION:** Apply online at www.western.edu/jobs. **Required attachments to the application include:** Letter of application, curriculum vitae, evidence of successful teaching and mentoring, evidence of successful scholarly or creative activity, and a reference list with names and contact information of three references, including from a current supervisor.

In compliance with the Colorado Job Application Fairness Act, in any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.

Please direct questions to Dr. Kevin Nelson, email: knelson@western.edu

**APPLICATION DEADLINE:** November 1, 2026. Review of applications will begin immediately.

**Additional Information on Western and Gunnison/Crested Butte**

Western Colorado University is a public institution with an enrollment of ~3,700 students. 47% of students are undergraduates, 33% are graduate students, and 80% receive some form of financial aid. Western students represent 17 countries, 50 states, and almost every county in Colorado. With an average class size of 17, Western’s faculty and staff share a strong commitment to personalized, rigorous, and immersive education. Visit http://www.western.edu to learn more about the university.

Western Colorado University is located in Gunnison, Colorado, about 200 miles southwest of Denver amidst over 2 million acres of public land and a vibrant ranching community. The Gunnison valley provides robust cultural programming and exceptional outdoor recreation. A network of dedicated community organizations enrich the lives of many in the tight-knit community. Living in the valley, one appreciates a vibrant culture of festivals, exhibitions, performances, wellness activities, and more. In the winter, many enjoy skiing at Crested Butte Mountain Resort and along dozens of miles of cross-country trails. In the summer, bikers, hikers, and runners explore 750-plus miles of singletrack trails, while others delight in fishing, boating, and paddleboarding at Blue Mesa Reservoir or on the Gunnison River and its tributaries. Pre-K-12 students are served by the highly-ranked Gunnison Watershed School District.

Western Colorado University encourages qualified candidates from all identities, backgrounds, and abilities to apply. Western is an equal opportunity employer committed to building inclusive, innovative work environments with employees who reflect our communities and enthusiastically serve them. Therefore, in all aspects of the employment process, we provide employment opportunities to all qualified applicants in accordance with applicable law.

*An Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability/vets.*

**WESTERN COLORADO UNIVERSITY IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER INCLUDING DISABILITY/VETERANS**

It is the ongoing policy and practice of Western Colorado University to provide equal opportunity in employment to all employees and applicants. No person shall be discriminated against in any condition of employment because of age (40 and over), color, disability, gender identity, genetic information, military or veteran status, national origin, ancestry, race, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression, marital status, or any other applicable status protected by federal, state, or local law.

**ADAAA ACCOMMODATIONS:**

Western Colorado University is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Western will assist individuals who have a disability with any reasonable accommodation requests related to employment, including completing the application process, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, participating in the employee selection process, and/or performing essential job functions where the requested accommodation does not impose an undue hardship. If you have a disability and require reasonable accommodation to ensure you have a positive experience applying or interviewing for this position, please direct your inquiries to the Office of Human Resources at HR@western.edu or (970) 943-3140.

  

### **About Us**

At Western Colorado University our faculty members and staff share a strong commitment to an inclusive and personalized education and take pride in following a set of values that form our vision as a university. Our shared values of courage, growth, inclusivity, integrity and stewardship provide the foundation for our culture and our work. Our faculty and staff are student-oriented, collegial, enthusiastic, and engaged in the campus and community. With the Rocky Mountains as our laboratory, Western is a premier public provider of rigorous, immersive education for our undergraduate and graduate students. The curriculum provides professional flexibility where experiential learning and interdisciplinary approaches are valued. Employees have chosen Western because of the quality of life combined with rewarding careers.

jobs.title: Tenure-Track: Assistant Professor in Artificial Intelligence and Animation
jobs.description:
##### **Description**

The Texas A&M University College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts (PVFA) and the Virtual Production Institute (VPI) invite applications for a full-time, 9-month tenure-track faculty position in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Animation at the rank of Assistant Professor within the Technical Arts and Interactive Media section. The anticipated start date is August 1, 2027.

Candidates should demonstrate strong potential for scholarly achievement and the ability to establish a nationally and internationally recognized research and/or creative works agenda in AI and Animation. We welcome applicants working broadly across animation, computer graphics, artificial intelligence, character animation, human motion, and related areas.

We are particularly interested in candidates whose research and/or creative works can advance performance capture and animation, broadly understood to include the capture, analysis, synthesis, modeling, and generation of expressive human and character movement. Relevant approaches may include motion capture, markerless and multimodal capture, AI-driven and generative motion models, computational performance, expressive character animation, real-time animation, and related emerging techniques.

Areas of expertise may include, but are not limited to:

* Animation craft and aesthetics, including performance, acting, timing, and character in animated movement

* Character animation and advanced animation techniques

* AI-driven animation, generative motion models, and neural representations

* Human motion analysis, synthesis, and computational performance

* Performance and motion capture in complex and real-time environments

* Markerless and multimodal capture approaches

* Expressive character movement and digital performance

* Applications in media and entertainment, virtual production, game-engine-based character performance, simulation and training, and other interdisciplinary domains

The successful candidate will be expected to establish an active program of research and/or creative works, pursue external funding opportunities, disseminate work through publications, presentations, exhibitions, software systems, patents, or other recognized scholarly outcomes, and contribute to the national and international visibility of PVFA and the VPI.

The successful candidate will also be expected to teach courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels, advise and mentor graduate students, participate in all aspects of PVFA's and the VPI's activities, and serve the professional community.

About the College

The College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts was formed in 2022 at Texas A&M University, bringing together the Department of Visualization, the Department of Performance Studies, and the Dance Science Program. PVFA is built without departments. Faculty sections and academic programs sit at the college level, which places musicians, composers, actors, directors, choreographers, dancers, painters, cinematographers, technical artists, level designers, spatial audio engineers, tools programmers, ethnomusicologists, art historians, UI/UX designers, and virtual set designers in one structure rather than in separate units. The College places a heavy emphasis on collaboration and interdisciplinary work in both scholarly and creative research.

The College offers the BS, MS, and MFA in Visualization, a PhD in Visual Computing and Interactive Media, and degree programs in music, dance, and theatre. It operates at the main campus in Bryan-College Station and as part of Texas A&M – Fort Worth, with facilities equipped for work at the intersection of the arts and emerging technology. Applicants should consult the college's website (https://pvfa.tamu.edu/) to review our academic and research programs.

About the Virtual Production Institute

This position is aligned with the mission of the Virtual Production Institute. Formed in 2023, the VPI is a technology-focused ecosystem for teaching, learning, and research. It develops emerging applications and the skilled workforce needed for virtual reality, augmented reality, sensors, projectors, and computing across multiple disciplines and industries. Its facilities in Bryan-College Station and Fort Worth include a performance capture and sound stage with supporting technology studio classrooms. Applicants should consult the institute's website (https://pvfa.tamu.edu/institutes/vpi/).

About the Ph.D. in Visual Computing and Interactive Media (VCIM)

The Ph.D. in Visual Computing and Interactive Media (VCIM) provides an interdisciplinary environment for advanced research at the intersection of computing, visualization, interactive media, and the arts. The program brings together faculty and students working across areas such as computer graphics, animation, artificial intelligence, visualization, virtual and augmented reality, interactive systems, and related creative and computational disciplines.

The successful candidate will have opportunities to advise VCIM doctoral students, develop graduate courses related to their research expertise, and collaborate across the College and the University on interdisciplinary research and creative projects. The successful candidate is expected to participate actively in the VCIM doctoral program, including advising Ph.D. students and, when eligible, chairing dissertation committees.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Environmental Design, Tenure Track
jobs.description:
Overview:

The School of Architecture, Planning and Landscape Architecture (APLA) at Auburn University, a comprehensive land-grant and research institution, invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in the Environmental Design program (ENVD) commencing August 2027.

For more than 118 years, APLA has educated designers across a range of allied fields while contributing to the region and the design professions through scholarship, creative practice, outreach, and community-engaged design. In addition to the Bachelor of Science in Environmental Design, APLA offers the Bachelor of Architecture, Master of Science in Architecture, Bachelor of Interior Architecture, Bachelor of Landscape Architecture, and Master of Landscape Architecture. The school’s commitment to public-interest design is exemplified by its two off-campus centers, Rural Studio in Hale County, Alabama, and Urban Studio in Birmingham, Alabama. As part of Auburn University’s College of Architecture, Design and Construction, APLA works alongside the McWhorter School of Building Science and the School of Industrial + Graphic Design to prepare future leaders in design and construction while fostering collaboration across the School, College, and broader University.

Auburn’s Environmental Design program brings together four interconnected units of study; Scenographies, Ecologies, Narratives, and Matters, to explore design across physical, digital, social, and environmental systems. Rather than treating the allied design disciplines of the school and college as a series of isolated domains, the ENVD program looks to overlap their methods and scales into an integrated approach of design inquiry and visualization allowing students to develop the ability to work across disciplinary boundaries and address complex spatial and cultural conditions. Through lab-based lectures, project-driven seminars, and immersive studio/workshops, students develop the critical and technical capacities necessary to navigate contemporary design practice. Preparation for study in these four units is supported through our program’s Design Core sequence of courses that serves as a foundation for student work to follow.

Responsibilities:

The primary responsibilities of the appointment include teaching, research, and service. Successful candidates for this position will be able to teach undergraduate workshops/studios, lecture courses, and/or seminars aligned with their area of focus in one of the program’s four units of study. They should demonstrate expertise in foundation and early design education, with a pedagogical approach that integrates an array of representation modes and interdisciplinary design methodologies. An ability to teach within and coordinate the Design Core sequence is essential, however an interest or research agenda situated in one or more of the program’s four units is welcomed and will be supported. Candidates will be expected to develop and maintain an active program of scholarly and/or creative work within the discipline. APLA is particularly interested in candidates who can contribute to the excellence of the academic community through their teaching, research, outreach, and service. Excellent interpersonal skills are required.

Review of applications will begin on **11 January 2027** and continue until the position is filled. If applicants have questions or need assistance in completing the application, including reasonable accommodations, including reasonable accommodations, please email Olivia Rodriguez: onr0002@auburn.edu

Environmental Design Faculty Search

School of Architecture, Planning, and Landscape Architecture

104 Dudley Hall

Auburn University, AL 36849

Qualifications:

**Minimum Qualifications:**

Candidates must hold a terminal degree in a design field at the time employment begins and present evidence of research/creative scholarship or the ability to develop and maintain an active research/creative scholarly program. The candidates selected for these positions must be able to meet eligibility requirements for work in the United States at the time of employment and continue working legally for the proposed term of employment. Auburn University is an EEO/VET/Disability Employer.

**Desired Qualifications:**

Desired qualifications include a demonstrated a focus on beginning design instruction, experience with contemporary drawing and modeling techniques (such as analog media, Rhino, Grasshopper, ArcGIS, or digital fabrication), experience in professional practice, experience in teaching, professional registration, and/or advanced degrees in Environmental Design or related fields. Salary will be commensurate with experience and qualifications.

**Required submission materials:**

* Combine into one document and upload your **letter of interest including delineation of pedagogical and research interest** and **current curriculum vitae** under the **“Resume Upload”** section (maximum files size: 5MB). All other documents should be uploaded under **“Additional Documents.”**

  

* 1) a letter of interest that identifies an area of teaching specialization and defines your scholarly plan
* 2) a curriculum vitae
* 3) names, addresses, telephone numbers, and email addresses of three referees
* 4) a print-ready portfolio containing professional, creative work and /or research, examples of prior teaching experience and sample student works. (12MB maximum)

If your digital portfolio exceeds the file size limit, please upload a Word document that includes a link to your portfolio.

Auburn University is understanding and sensitive to the family needs of faculty including dual-career couples. Please visit the following website for additional information: https://www.auburn.edu/academic/provost/pdf/guidelines-dual-career-services.pdf

Pay Range: USD $75,000.00 - USD $75,000.00 /Yr. Why Work at Auburn?:

* **Life-Changing Impact**: Our work changes lives through research, instruction, and outreach, making a lasting impact on our students, our communities, and the world.
* **Culture of Excellence**: We are committed to leveraging our strengths, resources, collaboration, and innovation as a top employer in higher education.
* **We’re Here for You**: Auburn offers generous benefits, educational opportunities, and a culture of support and work/life balance.
* **Sweet Home Alabama**: The Auburn/Opelika area offers southern charm, vibrant downtown scenes, top-ranked schools, and easy access to Atlanta, Birmingham, and the Gulf of Mexico beaches.
* **A Place for Everyone**: Auburn is committed to fostering an environment where all faculty, staff, and students are welcomed, valued, respected, and engaged.

**Ready to lead and shape the future of higher education? Apply today! War Eagle!**

Equal Opportunity Compliance Statement:

It is our policy to provide equal employment and education opportunities for all individuals without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, pregnancy, age, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other classification protected by applicable law. Please visit the Office of Equal Opportunity Compliance's website to learn more.

jobs.title: Associate Professor of Political Science - Oklahoma Baptist University
jobs.description:
Associate Professor of Political Science - Oklahoma Baptist University

**OBU Mission Statement**

OBU transforms lives by equipping students to pursue academic excellence, integrate faith with all areas of knowledge, engage a diverse world, and live worthy of the high calling of God in Christ.

**Expectations for all Employees**

Oklahoma Baptist University achieves its mission through a shared commitment to the following expectations. All employees must embrace these expectations and model them in their behavior.

* Demonstrate commitment to the essentials of the Christian faith.
* Commit to the mission and vision of Oklahoma Baptist University.
* Treat people with dignity and respect.
* Build relationships on honesty, integrity, and trust.
* Strive for excellence through teamwork, leadership, and a strong work ethic.
* Manage human and financial resources wisely and efficiently.

**Purpose:** Oklahoma Baptist University invites applications and nominations for a tenure-track position in Political Science, beginning August 2027. The successful candidate will teach American National Government, Introduction to Political Science, and upper-level courses in areas such as Congress, the courts, and the U.S. presidency. Other courses may be taught or developed according to the candidate’s expertise and departmental needs, subject to approval.

A Ph.D. in Political Science is strongly preferred by the time of appointment; advanced ABD candidates will be considered. Strong candidates will demonstrate excellence or strong promise in undergraduate teaching, student mentoring, and contributing to a rigorous liberal arts education within a Christian university context. The standard teaching load is 24 credit hours per academic year. Responsibilities also include advising Political Science majors and minors, participating in departmental, university, and professional service, and assisting with recruitment through meetings with prospective students and families.

The successful candidate will teach, advise, and serve in a manner consistent with Oklahoma Baptist University’s Christian mission and will thoughtfully integrate Christian faith with Political Science. The department especially welcomes candidates whose teaching and scholarship demonstrate respect for constitutional democracy, religious liberty, civil discourse, careful institutional analysis, and serious engagement with the Christian tradition.

Applicants should submit a letter of interest addressing their qualifications, teaching interests, and fit with Oklahoma Baptist University’s Christian mission. Additional materials should include a curriculum vitae, statement of teaching philosophy, statement of Christian faith, graduate transcripts, and a list of references. Review begins immediately and continues until filled.

**Essential Functions:**

* Teach introductory and upper-level undergraduate Political Science courses.

* Serve as an advisor to Political Science majors and minors.

* Keep accurate class records and submit reports and grades.

* Work regularly with faculty members from other disciplines.

* Keep regular office hours for advising students.

* Be an active member in a local evangelical church.

**Other Duties:**

* Maintain an active program of professional development.

* Assist in recruiting students to the Political Science program.

* Serve on university committees and take an active part in shaping the work of the division.

* Support and guide students in research and practica.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Must be able to teach multiple Political Science courses, including ones covering the major branches of the government.

* Possess and demonstrate strong interpersonal skills, communication skills, and pedagogy.

* Be able to conduct a college classroom to maximize the student learning experience.

* Be able to adjust teaching methods to meeting student needs.

* Be able to work effectively with college students in either individual advisement, as well as small and large class environments.

* Be able to relate to colleagues in the OBU community as well as be a representative to the professional community beyond OBU.

* Be proficient in office technology, office software (including various Microsoft tools), and classroom presentation software.

**Education:**

* **Required** : PhD in Political Science (advanced ABD considered).

* **Preferred** : Completed PhD in Political Science.

**Experience:**

* **Preferred:** Experience teaching undergraduates in a Christian, liberal arts environment.

**Special Requirements:**

* Must be a member of a local evangelical\* Christian church.

* Evangelical is a broad term referring to segment within Christianity which maintains the authority of the Bible and the belief in salvation by faith in Jesus alone.

**OBU Benefits Summary:**

OBU understands that our employees are our most valuable assets when fulfilling our mission. We strive to offer an extensive array of benefits and opportunities for employees to choose from. Full-time employees benefit from the generous OBU provision of premium contributions for nationwide family-friendly Health and Dental coverages along with free life insurance that includes accidental death and dismemberment equal to an employee’s base salary. OBU provides access to optional employee-paid ancillary benefits like vision, hospitalization, critical illness, accident, additional employee-paid family life insurance coverages, and education benefits at OBU and other institutions of higher education. There is generous paid time off that includes annual granted vacation time, accrued sick leave, six annual holidays, and week-long breaks for Thanksgiving and Christmas that include energy conservation days. For all employees working at least half-time, there is an employer matching opportunity for retirement investments in a 403(b)(9) plan administered by Guide Stone. There are numerous other perks and opportunities for OBU employees including FREE family membership to the OBU Recreation and Wellness Center or RAWC, Global outreach university mission trips, cafeteria discounts, and parking privileges to name a few.

jobs.title: Tenure-Track: Assistant Professor in Agriculture and Rural Community Leadership
jobs.description:
##### **Description**

The Department of Agricultural Leadership, Education, and Communications (ALEC) and College of Agriculture and Life Sciences at Texas A&M University invite applications for a full-time, 9-month Assistant Professor faculty position (tenure-track) with academic, scholarly, and faculty accomplishments in Agricultural and Rural Community Leadership. The anticipated start date for this opportunity is January 1, 2028.

The successful candidate will contribute to the continued growth of the ALEC academic programs, specifically the Agricultural Leadership (ALED) degree and the M.S. and Ph.D. degree programs in Agricultural Leadership, Education, and Communications. The position carries a Division of Effort of 50% research, 40% teaching, and 10% service. The individual in this position is expected to obtain federal, state, industrial, and/or foundation funding to support and sustain a vigorous research program.

Texas is simultaneously one of the most agriculturally productive and most unevenly developed states in the nation. It leads the country in cattle, cotton, hay, sheep, wool, goats, mohair, and horse production and ranks among the top ten producers for more than 40 major commodities. Yet the communities that anchor this agricultural economy face compounding pressures: a rural population of more than three million people who routinely struggle to access healthcare, broadband, education, and economic opportunity that urban counterparts take for granted. At least 74 Texas counties lack a hospital, 20 or more rural hospitals have closed since 2010, and nearly one million rural Texans lack adequate broadband connectivity, costing the state more than $5 billion in lost economic potential annually.

This position is designed to advance scholarship at the critical intersection of **agriculture** and **rural community leadership** **development**, recognizing that the strength of Texas’s commodity sectors and the vitality of its rural communities are deeply interdependent. Without capable local leaders navigating disruption, small towns and farm-dependent counties face decline; without thriving rural communities, the infrastructure, labor, and social capital that sustains commodity agriculture erodes.

The successful candidate will build a nationally recognized, externally funded research program examining how leaders of Texas’s agricultural commodity industries and rural communities are developed, prepared, and empowered to meet the challenges of 2030 and beyond.

**Research (50%)**

The successful candidate will:

* Develop and lead a vigorous, externally funded research program at the intersection of **agriculture** and **rural community leadership development**, with specific relevance to Texas’s agricultural commodity sectors and rural communities.
* Investigate leadership formation, capacity building, and organizational effectiveness within Texas agricultural commodity industries, such as beef cattle, cotton, corn, sorghum, poultry, dairy, sheep, goat, and specialty crop sectors.
* Pursue research on rural community leadership challenges facing Texas, such as community capacity building in farm-dependent counties; youth outmigration and succession of rural leadership; civic leadership development in small towns; rural economic diversification and entrepreneurship; and the leadership dimensions of rural health, broadband access, water systems, and infrastructure.
* Examine the intersections between commodity industry leadership and rural community wellbeing, including the roles of commodity organizations, producer cooperatives, and agricultural associations in sustaining rural communities.
* Pursue federal, state, industry, and foundation funding to sustain a productive research enterprise, including USDA NIFA, USDA AFRI, USDA Rural Development, Texas Department of Agriculture, Texas A&M AgriLife Research, commodity board partnerships, and private foundations.
* Produce peer-reviewed scholarship advancing knowledge at the intersection of leadership theory, rural community development, and agricultural systems.
* Engage directly with commodity leaders, producer organizations, rural community stakeholders, and municipal/county officials to ensure research relevance and promote knowledge transfer.
* Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams across ALEC, the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Texas A&M AgriLife Research, Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service, and partner institutions.
* Mentor and advise M.S. and Ph.D. students in the ALEC graduate programs.

**Teaching (40%)**

The successful candidate will:

* Teach undergraduate courses in the Agricultural Leadership and Development (ALED) degree program, with particular attention to courses in community leadership, organizational development, and civic engagement, consistent with the candidate’s areas of expertise. Additional coursework could be taught in courses associated with the International Agriculture minor.
* Develop and teach graduate-level courses in agricultural and rural community leadership for the M.S. and Ph.D. programs in ALEC.
* Advise and mentor undergraduate students, with particular attention to students enrolled in the ALEC Leadership Honors Program.
* Contribute curriculum development expertise to evolve academic offerings responsive to the leadership needs of Texas agricultural commodity industries and rural communities.

**Service (10%)**

The successful candidate will:

* Serve on departmental, college, and university committees as appropriate.
* Engage professionally through national organizations such as the American Association for Agricultural Education (AAAE), the Rural Sociological Society, or comparable entities.
* Participate in commodity organization advisory boards, industry task forces, rural community leadership programs, and producer leadership initiatives as opportunities arise.
* Contribute to community outreach through Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service, with possible engagement with the Texas Rural Leadership Program or similar statewide rural leadership initiatives.

**The Department**

The Department of Agricultural Leadership, Education, and Communications is a nationally recognized leader in the social sciences of agriculture and life sciences, housed in the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences at Texas A&M University. ALEC is home to approximately 1,300 undergraduate students, 300 graduate students, and more than 30 faculty scholars. ALEC faculty conduct impactful, interdisciplinary research that addresses critical issues pertaining to food, agriculture, natural resources, youth development, and human health, working where agriculture and the life sciences meet to strengthen both urban and rural communities in Texas, the nation, and worldwide.

ALEC offers undergraduate degrees in Agricultural Leadership and Development (ALED) and Agricultural Education (AGED), master’s and doctoral programs in Agricultural Leadership, Education, and Communications, and graduate certificates in Leadership Education Theory and Practice, Extension Education, International Agriculture, and Agriculture eLearning Development. A dedicated stream of ALEC research aims to improve the health, wellbeing, and livelihood of people living in rural areas, supporting initiatives, education, and programming to reinvigorate small towns, identify economic opportunities, and empower local citizens to lead and navigate change.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Architecture, Tenure Track
jobs.description:
Overview:

The School of Architecture, Planning and Landscape Architecture (APLA) at Auburn University, a comprehensive land-grant and research institution, invites applications for four tenure-track Assistant Professor positions in Architecture centered on teaching design studio and seminar/lecture courses commencing August 2027.

For more than 118 years, APLA has educated designers across a range of allied fields while contributing to the region and the design professions through scholarship, creative practice, outreach, and community-engaged design. In addition to the Bachelor of Science in Environmental Design, APLA offers the Bachelor of Architecture, Master of Science in Architecture, Bachelor of Interior Architecture, Bachelor of Landscape Architecture, and Master of Landscape Architecture. The school's commitment to public-interest design is exemplified by its two off-campus centers, Rural Studio in Hale County, Alabama, and Urban Studio in Birmingham, Alabama. As part of Auburn University's College of Architecture, Design and Construction, APLA works alongside the McWhorter School of Building Science and the School of Industrial + Graphic Design to prepare future leaders in design and construction while fostering collaboration across the School, College, and broader University.

Auburn's Architecture program engages design as cultural, social, technical, and environmental practice, preparing students to address the challenges and opportunities shaping the built environment. Through an integrated curriculum of design, history and theory, technology, and professional practice, students develop the ability to think critically across scalles, from building and cities to communities and regions. The program encourages collaboration with allied fields throughout the college and university fostering shared approaches to comples spatial, ecological, and societal questions. Through design studios, seminars, hands-on making, and research-based learning, students build the creative, analytical, and technical skills necessary for contemporary practice. Grounded in both experimentation and professional preparation, the program equips graduates to lead across varied modes of practice and to contribute to the future of the build environment.

**Position:**

The Architecture program seeks candidates whose design research/practice is rooted in architectural innovation. We welcome candidates engaged in a range of progressive practices or scholarship in architecture and allied fields. Applicants are expected to teach, conduct research/lead creative activity that contributes to or challenges current architectural thinking. The successful candidate will demonstrate how design can synthesize contemporary issues and disciplinary knowledge to cultivate students' architectural sensibilities, particularly in the design of buildings. We seek individuals who bring a strong design portfolio, a commitment to teaching excellence, and a clear vision for how architecture can engage with urgent disciplinary questions. The Architecture program seeks to fill four positions with teaching responsibilities to include design studio and seminars/lecture courses in one of the following areas of expertise: visual communication, representation, and design media; history and theory of architecture; and building technology, material innovation, and fabrication.

  
Responsibilities:

The primary responsibilities of the appointment include teaching, research, and service. Candidates will be expected to develop and maintain an active program of scholarly and/or creative work within the discipline. APLA is particularly interested in candidates who can contribute to the excellence of the academic community through their teaching, research, outreach, and service. Salary will be commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Qualifications:

**Required Qualifications:**

Candidates must hold a PhD, Master of Architecture, Master of Science in Architecture, or a Bachelor of Architecture plus a terminal degree in a related field, at the time employment begins. The candidates selected for these positions must be able to meet eligibility requirements for work in the United States at the time of employment and continue working legally for the term of employment. **Job Summary:**

Tenure Track Faculty members perform the functions of teaching, research or creative activities, and service and are assigned to an academic unit appropriate for their Discipline descriptor. Tenure Track Faculty members are usually hired as assistant professors and enter the tenure track. For example, an assistant professor must serve a probationary period of five years and be reviewed for tenure during his or her sixth year of continuous employment at the University. Tenure Track Faculty members may be hired, particularly at the associate and full ranks, with a reduction in the tenure probationary period, as explained in the Tenure Policy. Tenure Track Faculty members at the Associate and Full ranks are full members of the Graduate Faculty, while those at the Assistant rank are Associate Members of the Graduate Faculty.

**Job Description:**

The Department of Biology at the University of Mississippi invites applications for a 9-month tenure-track Assistant Professor position in the broad area of Quantitative Cell Biology. We seek candidates who use data-rich experimental approaches to study cells and to uncover molecular mechanisms across cellular, developmental, microbial, plant, organismal, and ecological systems.

  

We are especially interested in candidates with strong expertise in experimental approaches for measuring gene expression, gene regulation, and dynamic biological processes in living cells or multicellular organisms, who are prepared to lead an independent research program driven by fundamental science and curiosity-driven questions. Preferred approaches include quantitative live-cell imaging, optogenetics, advanced bioimage analysis, spatial and temporal gene expression measurements, phenomics, and AI-enabled analysis of biological data. This position should build upon the department’s existing strengths while significantly expanding its capacity in quantitative, mechanistic, and the integration of biology across scales and methods.

  

The Department of Biology is a broad-based department of 25 tenure-track and 21 instructional faculty members that educates over 900 undergraduate biology majors and more than 60 graduate students (Ph.D. and M.S.). More information about the department can be found at https://biology.olemiss.edu/.

**About the Department:**

Mason’s Communication Department has a diverse and collegial faculty committed to excellence, innovation, community and public service, inclusion, and social equity. All department faculty participate in the life of our campus community, including career fairs, faculty functions, recruiting sessions and other events. Located just 15 miles from Washington, D.C., we offer a broad undergraduate program with more than 300 majors; six minor programs; a vibrant MA program including strategic communication; health communication; science, environment, and risk communication; and media and culture specialties; and a highly ranked PhD program emphasizing health; strategic; and science, environment, and risk communication. The department also offers a graduate certificate in science communication. We serve a diverse population of undergraduate and graduate students who bring a wide variety of cultures and backgrounds to our classrooms. Additionally, the department supports several co-curricular activities, including debate, forensics, Public Relations Student Society of America (PRSSA), Society of Professional Journalists (SPJ), and a comprehensive student media program.
  
  
The research life of the department includes both undergraduate and graduate research and is reflected in the activities and outreach of its faculty, including those of the Center for Climate Change Communication (4C); the Communication, Health, and Relational Media (CHARM) research lab; the Center for Health and Risk Communication (CHRC); the Pop Culture lab; and the Character Assassination and Reputation Politics (CARP) research lab, in addition to several university-wide research centers and institutes including the Institute for Digital Innovation.
  
  
For more information on the Department of Communication at George Mason University, visit communication.gmu.edu.

**About the Position:**

The Department of Communication in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences at George Mason University seeks a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor of Communication, with a specialty in new/emerging communication technology and innovative research methods.

Applicants should have a PhD in Communication or a closely related field. We welcome candidates from any communication subfield. We are especially interested in those whose work engages one or more of our core areas: strategic communication and public relations; health communication; science, environment, and risk communication; media studies; journalism; or advocacy and political communication. The successful candidate will demonstrate an active research agenda focused on new/emerging communication technologies with innovative research methods, a record of competitive conference papers and/or scholarly publications commensurate with experience, an ongoing research agenda, a commitment to excellence in teaching and mentoring a diverse student body, and a willingness to contribute to departmental and university service. We welcome all methodological approaches and specifically seek a candidate who pursues innovative methods to examine and/or utilize new and emerging technology. Candidates should demonstrate an ability to teach graduate and undergraduate courses in a variety of areas, as listed above. Overall, teaching experience at the university level is preferred. Finally, an interest in developing curriculum and courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels is also preferred.

**Responsibilities:**

* Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in communication, including courses related to new and emerging technologies;
* Mentor and advise students;
* Develop and maintain an active research agenda focused on new and emerging communication technologies using innovative research methods; and
* Contribute to departmental, college, university, and professional service through committee participation, faculty governance, program and curriculum activities, and service to the discipline.

**Required Qualifications:**

* PhD in communication, or related field, completed prior to appointment;
* Active research agenda grounded in the study of new/emergent media, with a record of competitive conference papers and/or published research commensurate with experience;
* Demonstration of quantitative or qualitative innovative research methods, such as advanced natural language processing (NLP) and text mining (AI content analysis), digital ethnography, online social network analysis, AI content generation, social media analytics and big data analysis, agent-based modeling, or other innovative technological approaches to research;
* Ability to teach courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels that contribute to our subareas as listed above;
* Ability to teach theory courses in new media and technology and within the candidate’s particular subfield of communication;
* Commitment to teaching and mentoring a diverse student community; and
* Commitment to service for the department, university, and discipline.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* PhD in communication (rather than a PhD in a related field);
* A record of relevant published research commensurate with experience;
* Relevant teaching experience at the college or university level;
* Experience with or interest in developing courses and curriculum at undergraduate and graduate levels; and
* Experience with or interest in undergraduate student mentoring and graduate student advising.

Cover letter  
Curriculum vitae  
Brief statement of teaching philosophy that includes interest in specific courses in the polymer science and engineering undergraduate and graduate curricula and discusses approaches to laboratory, design, experiential learning, and integration of professional practice into the curriculum.  
Name and contact information for at least three references (letters will be requested following initial review).  
  
Review of applications will begin November 20, 2026 and continue until the position is filled. Applications received after this date may be considered at the discretion of the committee and/or hiring authority.  
  
For inquiries, contact Dr. Derek Patton, Director, School of Polymer Science and Engineering at derek.patton@usm.edu.  
  
Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without the need for visa sponsorship. The University will not sponsor applicants for work visas (e.g., H-1B).  
  
**Job Summary**  
The School of Polymer Science and Engineering (SPSE) at The University of Southern Mississippi invites applications for a full-time, nine-month, non-tenure-track Professor of Practice position beginning August 2027. We seek candidates with strong technical expertise and professional experience in polymer science and engineering who will contribute to the School’s teaching, experiential learning, student mentoring, and industry engagement activities.  
  
The successful candidate will teach undergraduate courses in polymer science and engineering, with opportunities to teach graduate courses, particularly emphasizing laboratory, design, and other applied aspects of the curriculum. In this role, the successful candidate will draw on professional practice and applied experience to strengthen classroom and elevate experiential learning, while supporting student professional development and engagement with industry and other external partners.  
  
Opportunities also exist to engage in and support the broader research enterprise of the School, including participation in externally funded projects, applied research, workforce development, and industry-sponsored activities.  
  
**Primary Duties and Responsibilities**

* Teach undergraduate and as appropriate, graduate courses in polymer science and engineering.
* Develop and deliver laboratory, prototyping, design-based, and other experiential learning activities.
* Advise and mentor students through capstone design, applied projects, and other project-based educational experiences.
* Mentor undergraduate students in academic, professional, and career development.
* Collaborate with faculty and staff on curriculum development, assessment, accreditation, workforce development, outreach, and industry engagement.
* Build and strengthen relationships with industry and government partners in support of education, experiential learning, workforce development, and collaborative activities.
* Contribute to grant writing, proposal development, and externally funded projects, particularly those involving applied research, workforce development, or industry partnerships.
* Contribute to the mission of the School, College, University, and broader professional community through service.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

  

**Minimum Qualifications**  
Earned Ph.D. in polymer science and engineering or a closely related discipline.  
Professional experience in industry, government, applied research, or a closely related setting relevant to polymer science and engineering.  
  
**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

* Ability to work effectively, collaboratively, and collegially with students, staff, faculty, and external partners.
* Ability to apply polymer science and engineering fundamentals to practical problems and applications.
* Knowledge of common polymer characterization, processing, testing, and laboratory methods.
* Ability to translate professional practice and applied technical experience into effective classroom, laboratory, and project-based instruction.
* Ability to contribute to curriculum development, assessment, and continuous improvement.
* Strong written and oral communication skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**  
Three or more years of professional experience in industry, government, applied research, manufacturing, or a related setting relevant to polymer science and engineering.  
Prior teaching, training, or student mentorship experience in higher education, industry, or another professional setting.  
Demonstrated ability to integrate professional or industry practice into teaching, experiential learning, and student mentorship.  
Experience with polymer processing, manufacturing, product development, scale-up, testing, or characterization.  
Experience advising design projects or multidisciplinary design-build-test activities.  
Familiarity with ABET accreditation and outcomes-based assessment.  
Experience contributing to externally funded, industry-sponsored, workforce development, or applied research activities.  
Demonstrated ability to develop productive relationships with industry or government partners.  
  
**About the School**  
The School of Polymer Science and Engineering (SPSE) is one of the nation's few academic units devoted entirely to polymer science and engineering. SPSE comprises 13 faculty members, including multiple early-career awardees. Research in the School spans polymer composites and materials for extreme environments, including fire-retardant and carbon–carbon systems; biomaterials and polymers for human health, including tissue repair, regeneration, and therapeutic delivery; materials for energy and sustainability; optoelectronic materials; and advanced coatings. SPSE maintains a robust, well-funded research portfolio supported by federal agencies, industry, and private foundations. The Thames Polymer Science Research Center provides state-of-the-art facilities for polymer research, including NMR (400/600 MHz), TEM, SAXS/WAXS, XPS/UPS, polymer processing (extrusion/injection molding), composite fabrication, and advanced thermal, rheological, and mechanical characterization tools.  
  
SPSE sustains one of the largest polymer-focused graduate programs in the country alongside a growing ABET-accredited undergraduate program, and offers B.S., M.S., and Ph.D. degrees in polymer science and engineering. For more information about SPSE, visit usm.edu/polymer-science-engineering.

**About The University of Southern Mississippi**
  
Since our founding in 1910, The University of Southern Mississippi has remained dedicated to preparing students for success. We deliver programs to more than 13,000 students in Hattiesburg and Long Beach, at teaching and research sites across the Mississippi Gulf Coast, as well as online. We are a community-engaged Carnegie R1 university, earning distinction as one of the nation's leading research institutions.  
  
Southern Miss is known for pioneering work in polymer science, ocean science, spectator sports safety and security, and bringing language to children with communication disorders. We are also a national leader in a broad range of disciplines, including cybersecurity, hydrography, nutrition, aquaculture, kinesiology, and economic development, among others.
  
  
We produce graduates ready to enter fields that are leading the way in emerging technologies through programs such as computer engineering, information technology, and ocean engineering. We’re developing the next generation of business leaders, while also responding to critical workforce shortages by producing skilled professionals in education and nursing. With a tradition of excellence in the arts, we are one of only 36 public institutions in the nation accredited in four major areas of the arts. Home to the Golden Eagles, our student-athletes compete in 17 NCAA Division I sports. With a culture marked by passion and persistence, Southern Miss is delivering graduates who are ready for life. For more information, visit www.usm.edu.

LaGrange College seeks to fill a tenure-track position at the assistant professor level in Religious Studies beginning August 1, 2027. The field of specialization is open, but preference will be given to candidates who can teach Christian ethics and broader philosophical approaches to ethics including Bioethics and possibly business ethics and the ethics of AI, as well as candidates prepared to contribute in areas such as American Christianity or world religious traditions.
  
  
A Ph.D. in religious studies or related field is required, although outstanding ABD candidates will be considered. The successful candidate must have their terminal degree completed prior to the end of their second year in the position.
  
  
The teaching load is four (4) courses per semester, including introductory courses, upper-level electives in the candidate’s field(s) of specialization, and courses that satisfy the college’s general education curriculum, known as Ethos. The position includes the supervision and mentorship of undergraduate research projects in the field. Candidates should demonstrate a commitment to excellence in teaching, professional development, and institutional service, as well as an understanding of, and appreciation for, the mission of liberal arts institutions.

jobs.title: Tenure-Track: Assistant Professor of Art & Design in Intelligent Systems and Computational Design
jobs.description:
##### **Description**

The Texas A&M University College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts (PVFA) invites applications for a tenure-track, full-time, 9-month Assistant Professor of Art & Design in Intelligent Systems and Computational Design position in the Art & Design (ARTD) Section of the Visualization Program. The anticipated start date is August 1, 2027.

The ARTD Section seeks an artist and/or designer whose work advances contemporary creative practice by blending intelligent systems, computational design, and generative methodologies as primary modes of artistic and design inquiry. We are particularly interested in candidates whose creative and scholarly work explores generative systems, machine learning, creative coding, computational creativity, and emerging forms of AI-enabled artistic and design production.

We seek candidates whose work investigates the creative, cultural, aesthetic, and critical possibilities of machine learning, generative AI, algorithmic systems, computational visualization, procedural design, and related computational approaches to art and design.

The Section welcomes research and creative practice across areas including:

* Artificial Intelligence and Creative Practice
    
  Creative applications of intelligent systems and machine learning, human-AI collaboration, computational creativity, and emerging approaches to artistic and design production.

* Computational Design
    
  Algorithmic design, creative coding, procedural systems, computational visualization, generative workflows, and computational methods for design innovation.

* Critical and Experimental Futures
    
  Research and creative work, including publications, that examines the cultural, social, ethical, and aesthetic implications of AI and computational technologies.

Across these areas, we are interested in how computation functions not simply as a tool, but as a medium for artistic inquiry, design research, experimentation, and creative production. We are particularly interested in candidates who demonstrate how intelligent systems, generative methodologies, and computational design function as conceptual, aesthetic, and material frameworks for contemporary artistic and design practice.

Computational and AI-driven practices may result in a wide range of outcomes, including screen-based experiences, physical artifacts, fabricated objects, spatial installations, immersive environments, performances, and hybrid digital-physical works. Physical making and material experimentation are welcomed as potential manifestations of computational practice but are neither required nor privileged over other forms of creative output.

Consistent with the interdisciplinary mission of the College, we value candidates who demonstrate the ability to collaborate across art, design, visualization, computing, engineering, architecture, the humanities, performance, and the performing arts to produce meaningful creative, scholarly, and public-facing work.

The successful candidate will develop and maintain an active, externally recognized program of creative practice and/or research; contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching in intelligent systems, computational design, generative creative practice, and contemporary art and design methodologies; mentor undergraduate and graduate students; develop innovative curriculum; and contribute to academic service.

The successful candidate will be expected to teach undergraduate and graduate courses aligned with their areas of expertise, which may include artificial intelligence for creative practice, generative design, computational design, creative coding, computational visualization, digital fabrication, digital sculpture, and studio-based creative practice; advise and mentor MFA students; contribute to the continued evolution of graduate studio-based research and creative practice within the Visualization Program; participate in collaborative and interdisciplinary activities; and serve the profession, the program, and the university community.

About the College

The College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts was formed in 2022 at Texas A&M University, bringing together the Department of Visualization, the Department of Performance Studies, and the Dance Science Program. PVFA is built without departments. Faculty sections and academic programs sit at the college level, which places musicians, composers, actors, directors, choreographers, dancers, painters, cinematographers, technical artists, level designers, spatial audio engineers, tools programmers, ethnomusicologists, art historians, UI/UX designers, and virtual set designers in one structure rather than in separate units. The College places a heavy emphasis on collaboration and interdisciplinary work in both scholarly and creative research.

The College offers the BS, MS, and MFA in Visualization, a PhD in Visual Computing and Interactive Media, and degree programs in music, dance, and theatre. It operates at the main campus in Bryan-College Station and as part of Texas A&M – Fort Worth, with facilities equipped for work at the intersection of the arts and emerging technology. Applicants should consult the college's website (https://pvfa.tamu.edu/) to review our academic and research programs.

The Texas A&M University College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts (PVFA) invites applications for a full-time, 9-month tenure-track position in Theatrical Production Management and Research at the rank of Assistant Professor in the Dance, Music, and Theatre Performance section. The anticipated start date is August 1, 2027.

Candidates should demonstrate strong potential for scholarly achievement and an ability to establish a nationally and internationally recognized agenda for research and creative work focused on producing and researching structures that make interdisciplinary, virtual/hybrid, media-integrated, and devised performance possible. Areas of expertise may include, but are not limited to:

* Digital Transformation and Technology

* producing and scheduling systems for media-integrated and technology-driven performance

* live streaming, virtual and hybrid producing models

* data analytics for production planning, budgeting, and audience/venue operations

* Collaborative and Non-hierarchical Producing Models

* producing structures for devised and collectively created work, where authorship and decision-making are distributed rather than script-first

* Sound and Media Design as Producing Practice

* sound design, projection/media design, and live media integration as both creative and infrastructural components of production

* Interdisciplinary Partnerships

* producing collaborations across the theatre, dance, music, and visualization programs

* engaging with emerging technology across PVFA

This position supports the College's Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre, a practice-based, devised-theatre program established in Fall 2024, and complements the program's existing technical design faculty. Successful candidates will teach Stage Management and Producing Theatre and other courses as assigned that fall within their expertise. Preference will be given to candidates who also have experience in sound and/or new media design and an interest in advancing those design dimensions of the program.

The successful candidate will be expected to:

* Establish an active, nationally and internationally visible program of research and/or creative practice investigating production management as a discipline of its own — including its digital, collaborative, and technological dimensions

* Disseminate work through exhibitions, performances, publications, presentations, software systems, patents, or other recognized scholarly outcomes

* Contribute production-management expertise to PVFA's theatre curriculum and season, and possibly sound and/or new media design expertise, as a site for applied research and graduate/undergraduate mentorship

* Build interdisciplinary partnerships that extend production-management research into visualization, data science, or technology domains represented elsewhere in the College

* Contribute to section, college, and university service

The College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts was formed in 2022 at Texas A&M University, bringing together the Department of Visualization, the Department of Performance Studies, and the Dance Science Program. Faculty sections and academic programs sit at the college level, which places musicians, composers, actors, directors, choreographers, dancers, painters, cinematographers, technical artists, level designers, spatial audio engineers, tools programmers, ethnomusicologists, art historians, UI/UX designers, and virtual set designers in one structure rather than in separate units. The College places a heavy emphasis on collaboration and interdisciplinary work in both scholarly and creative research.

The College offers the BS, MS, and MFA in Visualization, a PhD in Visual Computing and Interactive Media, and degree programs in music, dance, and theatre. jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor in Energy Innovation - Engineering
jobs.description:
Req Id: 44435

Job Title: Assistant/Associate Professor in Energy Innovation - Engineering

City: West Lafayette

**Job Summary**
---------------

Purdue Engineering invites applications for multiple tenure/tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor positions as part of a cluster hire in energy innovation at our West Lafayette location, led by Purdue’s Institute for Energy Innovation (IEI) . IEI brings together faculty, students, industry, government, and community partners to develop industry-driven energy solutions. IEI seeks to ensure the availability of abundant, reliable, and affordable energy; advance U.S. energy leadership and domestic supply-chain resilience; and accelerate the translation of research into technologies that are technically sound, commercially viable, and economically scalable. Its activities are organized around five major initiatives: Grid of Tomorrow, Nuclear Energy, Battery and Energy Storage, Geothermal and Natural Gas, and Critical Materials.

  

Through this cluster hire, Purdue Engineering seeks exceptional candidates whose research interests and expertise align with one or more of the following initiatives or the crosscutting research themes described below. Research topics include, but are not limited to, the examples below:

  

1. **Grid of Tomorrow** : Power systems research to modernize the electrical grid, including grid planning and operations with large data center and industrial loads; grid data analytics and artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML); grid flexibility; large-scale integration of distributed energy resources and storage; power electronics; protection; and power system dynamics.

2. **Nuclear Energy** : Nuclear power technologies, including small modular reactors and microreactors for distributed energy generation and industrial applications; advanced reactor technologies, nuclear materials, and the nuclear fuel cycle; fusion and plasma engineering; tritium production, handling, and management; and integration of nuclear energy with electrical grids and industrial energy systems.

3. **Battery and Energy Storage** : Resilient and sustainable energy-storage architectures; next-generation battery chemistries, including those using earth-abundant materials; and storage solutions for electrified mobility, aviation, defense, and the electrical grid. Across these areas, topics of interest include novel metrology, characterization, analytics, predictive modeling, safety, recycling, and scalable manufacturing.

4. **Geothermal and Natural Gas** : Technologies that provide reliable and abundant sources of electricity, industrial heat, and fuels, including geothermal resource development and energy systems; efficient utilization and catalytic conversion of natural gas and light hydrocarbons; carbon management; and engines and combined heat and power.

5. **Critical Materials** : Materials innovation and resilient domestic supply chains for energy technologies, including the discovery, design, synthesis, characterization, recovery, separation, purification, recycling, and scalable manufacturing of critical materials used in batteries, magnets, semiconductors, nuclear systems, and other energy technologies, as well as alternatives that reduce dependence on scarce materials.

  

Across these initiatives, we welcome research on **Energy Utilization** , including heat pumps and industrial efficiency. Examples include technologies that improve energy efficiency in chemical, cement, and steel processing. We also welcome research on energy systems integration and engineering approaches that incorporate techno-economic analysis, energy markets, supply chains, and deployment. Opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and industry engagement are central to IEI’s mission.

**Qualifications**
------------------

Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a closely related discipline by the start of employment. Early-career applicants should show evidence of initiating independent research, while mid-career applicants should demonstrate a sustained record of independent research within academic or industrial organizations, and contributions to education and/or mentoring. Successful candidates will be expected to conduct original research, attract external research support, advise graduate students, teach undergraduate and graduate courses, and contribute service to their academic unit, the College of Engineering, Purdue University, and the broader profession.

  

Appointments will be made in the academic school within Purdue’s College of Engineering that most closely aligns with each candidate’s background and research expertise. Applicants interested in a position in any of Purdue’s engineering schools are welcome to apply. Successful candidates will also engage with IEI and collaborate across disciplines to develop research and education programs and partnerships in energy innovation.

**Institute and College**
-------------------------

The Institute for Energy Innovation connects Purdue’s strengths in engineering and science with expertise in business, economics, and policy. Through interdisciplinary research, hands-on education, and partnerships with industry, government, and national laboratories, IEI helps faculty translate fundamental discoveries into practical energy technologies. Its industry engagement brings research needs and deployment challenges into academic collaborations and prepares students to contribute to the energy workforce. Purdue Engineering is renowned for top-notch faculty and students, unique research facilities and innovations, and a culture of collegiality and persistent pursuit of preeminence. As one of the top ranked and largest engineering colleges in the nation, we are the first among U.S. engineering colleges in annual graduates and market demand, and have 8 degree programs ranked in the top 10 nationally. Purdue Engineering is a top-ranked college for patents and translation of our research activities to practice in the state, nation, and world. More than 70 Purdue Engineering faculty and alumni are National Academy of Engineering members, and we look to continue bringing outstanding faculty to campus, remaining the leader in affordable excellence at scale by guiding strategic growth through investment in people, exciting initiatives , and facilities .

**Application Process**
-----------------------

Applicants should submit the following materials to this site:

  

1. A cover letter identifying the IEI initiative or initiatives, or crosscutting research themes, most closely aligned with the applicant’s expertise and the engineering school of primary interest;

2. A complete curriculum vitae;

3. A research statement (maximum two pages, excluding references) describing the applicant’s research accomplishments and future plans, including their alignment with IEI and opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and technology translation;

4. A teaching statement (maximum two pages, excluding references) describing the applicant’s interests and approach to undergraduate and graduate education and student mentoring; and

5. The names and contact information of at least four references.

  

Review of applications will begin on November 9, 2026 and will continue until the positions are filled. Questions regarding the positions or application process may be directed to Purdue Engineering Academic Affairs, coeacademicaffairs@purdue.edu . A background check is required for employment in these positions.

  

Purdue University and the College of Engineering offer a Concierge Program that provides dual-career assistance and relocation services.

  

*Purdue University is an equal opportunity/equal access university.*
