jobs.description:
The Department of Computer Science at the University of Virginia (UVA) invites applications for multiple tenured or tenure-track faculty positions at all ranks.

We seek outstanding researchers and educators who will contribute to the continued growth, excellence, and intellectual breadth of the Department. The Department has substantial research strengths spanning artificial intelligence and machine learning, computer systems, architecture, cyber-physical systems, human-centered computing, robotics and autonomous systems, security, privacy, and cryptography, software engineering and programming languages, and algorithms and theory. We are particularly interested in candidates who will enhance and connect with the university’s AI research initiatives in both foundational and applied AI research, but also welcome applications across the full spectrum of computer science, including foundational research, emerging areas of computing, interdisciplinary research, and work that creates connections across established fields.

The primary responsibilities for these tenured/tenure-track positions include developing an internationally recognized research program, teaching and mentoring, and service to the department, university, public, and professional community. The appointment rank will be commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Our department is proud of its strong culture of collaboration and collegiality and is committed to sustaining and strengthening it. Faculty collaborate extensively throughout the School of Engineering and Applied Science and with colleagues in UVA’s Schools of Data Science, Medicine, Nursing, Law, Public Policy, Business, Education, and Arts & Sciences. These connections foster opportunities for foundational and interdisciplinary research spanning computing, science, engineering, health, and society.

Computer Science plays a key role in several major interdisciplinary research efforts at UVA. The Department is a founding member of the Link Lab, a multidisciplinary research center bringing together researchers in computer science, electrical and computer engineering, mechanical and aerospace engineering, and systems engineering to advance cyber-physical systems, robotics, autonomous systems, and the Internet of Things. CS faculty are also deeply engaged with UVA’s Biocomplexity Institute, university-wide efforts in artificial intelligence and data science, and interdisciplinary initiatives spanning health, biotechnology, neuroscience, and digital technology and society.

UVA is making substantial investments in computing and artificial intelligence research, including state-of-the-art high-performance computing and GPU infrastructure for large-scale AI, machine learning, data analytics, and computational science, and university-wide AI initiatives for researchers at all stages. These investments complement a growing university-wide community working on both the foundations of AI and its applications across science, engineering, health, and society.

The Department offers Ph.D. and master’s degrees through the School of Engineering and Applied Science and bachelor’s degrees through both the School of Engineering and Applied Science and the College of Arts & Sciences. Computer Science also collaborates with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering to jointly administer UVA’s undergraduate and graduate Computer Engineering programs.

UVA is a highly selective undergraduate and graduate institution and one of the nation’s leading public universities. UVA is situated in the beautiful city of Charlottesville, Virginia, a picturesque and vibrant small city consistently recognized as one of the nation's top places to reside. UVA's location offers proximity to Washington D.C., enriching opportunities for collaboration and engagement with numerous federal organizations. More information about the city, the school, faculty benefits and other topics can be found at https://hr.virginia.edu/careers-uva/why-uva .

In conjunction with these positions, senior graduate students are eligible and encouraged to consider the UVA Engineering Rising Scholars program. This program is designed to encourage early-career scholars to pursue a career in academia by supporting their postdoctoral work before beginning a tenure-track position at the University of Virginia. Detailed information and application instructions are available at https://engineering.virginia.edu/rising-scholars-postdoctoral-program

  

Candidates must have received a doctorate or equivalent in a computing field by the start of their appointment. Evidence of a commitment to high-impact scholarship, funded research, undergraduate- and graduate-level teaching and advising excellence, professional and university service, and mentoring are expected.

  

Applications should be submitted via Interfolio . Review of applications will begin on November 15, 2026. The application package must include:

* a cover letter
* a curriculum vitae
* research statement
* teaching philosophy statement
* service statement
* three representative research papers;

In addition, the names and contact information of at least three individuals that can serve as references should be provided.

The University will perform background checks on all new faculty hires prior to making a final offer of employment.

For questions about these positions, please contact Ferdinando Fioretto, Associate Professor, at fioretto@virginia.edu .

jobs.title: 4-H Youth Development Extension Agent - Club and Volunteer Development
jobs.description:
The WVU Extension Service is seeking a dynamic individual who will provide statewide leadership for 4-H Club and Volunteer Development programs. This position will lead efforts related to 4-H club development, volunteer management, compliance, chartering, special interest programs, volunteer training, program evaluation, and resource development. The position serves youth, volunteers, Extension professionals, and communities across West Virginia through educational programming, organizational development, and volunteer leadership initiatives. This is a statewide faculty position. The position carries the academic rank of Service Instructor or Service Assistant Professor, depending upon the candidate’s level of education. This is a twelve-month, full-time, promotable, non-tenure-track appointment.

**Major Responsibilities**

This position is primarily dedicated to serving youth, volunteers, communities, the state, the university, and the broader profession through the development, delivery, and evaluation of educational programs related to 4-H clubs, special interest programs, and volunteer development.

The successful candidate will provide statewide leadership for 4-H club and volunteer systems through educational programming, volunteer development, compliance oversight, partnership development, fiscal stewardship, and program evaluation.

The position is responsible to the State 4-H Program Director for all programmatic and administrative matters. The faculty member will work collaboratively with county Extension personnel, state Extension specialists, the WVU Extension Office of Volunteer Management, Compliance, and Development, community partners, and national organizations to strengthen and expand club-based and volunteer-led youth development programming throughout West Virginia.

**Functions and Tasks**

* Conduct educational programs in their designated program area to help people more effectively interpret and use science-based findings.
* Assume responsibility for developing, implementing, and evaluating a statewide Plan of Work for 4-H Club and Volunteer Development programming.
* Provides statewide leadership for 4-H club development, special interest programs, volunteer engagement, volunteer management systems, and organizational sustainability.
* Lead and coordinate statewide, interstate, and international 4-H youth development initiatives that promote leadership, citizenship, cultural competency, and community engagement.
* Collaborates with faculty, staff, volunteers, youth, and stakeholders to assess educational needs, identify priorities, and develop innovative educational opportunities that support statewide program goals.
* Review, revise, develop, and disseminate educational resources, curricula, and support materials for 4-H clubs, special interest programs, volunteers, and Extension professionals.
* Identify, recruit, train, support, and recognize volunteers who contribute to the successful delivery of 4-H club and special interest programming.
* Provide leadership for volunteer growth, retention, succession planning, and recognition initiatives across the state.
* Serve as the statewide leader for 4-H club chartering and Memoranda of Understanding (MOU) processes, ensuring compliance with established policies and procedures.
* Support youth protection and volunteer vetting processes in collaboration with the WVU Extension Vetting Team and the Office of Volunteer Management, Compliance, and Development.
* Plan, coordinate, and administer statewide contests, demonstrations, trainings, conferences, recognition events, and other program activities that advance positive youth development. This includes prominent events in Communication and Expressive Arts, fostering youth development.
* Develop and utilize effective systems for reporting program accomplishments, documenting outcomes, evaluating impacts, and demonstrating public value.
* Secure financial resources through grants, fundraising efforts, sponsorships, and partnerships to support program growth and sustainability.
* Provide leadership and guidance regarding fiscal management, tax exemption policies, financial accountability, and best practices for 4-H clubs and affiliated groups.
* Function at all times as a professional educator, maintaining high standards of teaching, scholarship, service, and stakeholder engagement.

**Service**

* Develop an understanding of the state, the needs of its citizens, and Extension’s role in meeting those needs.
* Develop and maintain a comprehensive understanding of youth development, volunteer engagement, organizational development, and community leadership needs throughout West Virginia.
* Serve as the statewide subject matter expert for 4-H club development, volunteer management, chartering, compliance, and special interest programs.
* Continuously evaluate and refine their role as an educator, leader, and change agent in strengthening volunteer-led youth programming across the state.
* Assess the degree to which programs meet the needs of youth, volunteers, Extension professionals, and stakeholders while promoting meaningful learning and behavioral change.
* Evaluate the effectiveness and impacts of educational programs and organizational systems related to clubs, volunteers, and youth engagement.
* Demonstrate the ability to apply current research, emerging trends, and best practices related to volunteer development, youth leadership, organizational management, and positive youth development.
* Work collaboratively with county Extension offices, schools, community organizations, state and federal agencies, and regional and national partners to strengthen programming opportunities.
* Serve as West Virginia’s liaison for regional and national initiatives related to 4-H clubs, volunteer development, and special interest programs.
* Participate in professional development activities that enhance expertise in youth development, volunteer management, educational program delivery, and organizational leadership.
* Provide mentorship and support to new Extension faculty and staff regarding effective club management, volunteer engagement, and program implementation.
* Support youth recruitment, retention, and student success efforts by creating educational experiences, workforce development opportunities, leadership pathways, and career exploration activities that encourage future enrollment at WVU and other post-secondary institutions.

**Teaching**

* Conduct needs assessments and engage community partners to identify priorities, mobilize resources, and develop, coordinate, and deliver research-based educational programs that meet the needs of citizens and communities.
* Develop, market, deliver, facilitate, and evaluate statewide educational programs focused on 4-H club development, volunteer leadership, organizational management, compliance, fiscal stewardship, and positive youth development.
* Establish clear educational objectives and utilize appropriate research-based subject matter and educational resources to achieve program goals and desired outcomes.
* Select, adapt, develop, and disseminate research-based curricula, training materials, and educational resources aligned with state and national 4-H priorities.
* Design and implement a variety of educational delivery methods, including trainings, workshops, conferences, webinars, volunteer development programs, and outreach activities to serve diverse audiences.
* Provide educational leadership and support to Extension professionals, volunteers, families, and community partners to ensure consistent and effective delivery of high-quality 4-H programming.
* Develop volunteer training and professional development opportunities that strengthen program quality, safety, accountability, and sustainability.
* Evaluate program effectiveness, measure participant outcomes and program impacts, and report accomplishments and public value to stakeholders and university leadership.
* Uses evaluation findings, stakeholder feedback, and emerging research to continuously improve program quality, relevance, accessibility, and impact.
* Understand the philosophy of Extension and utilize effective methodology in program delivery and evaluation.
* Understand and convey the philosophy, objectives and policies of WVUES.
* Assist in determining and obtaining resources needed to implement the Plan of Work.
* Plan and provide the training needed to equip volunteer leaders to carry out the program.
* Develop and maintain two-way communications with volunteer leaders.
* Understand and implement the provisions of EEO and ADA.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* For appointment at the Service Assistant Professor rank, the applicant must have a master’s degree.
* For appointment at the Service Instructor rank, the applicant must have a bachelor’s degree.
* Current West Virginia University faculty members who are selected for this position may be eligible to transfer their existing rank and tenure status, as appropriate and subject to University policies and procedures.
* Candidates with a degree in progress may be considered for this position, but the degree must be conferred by the hire date.
* Desirable areas of educational experience and training include youth development, Extension education, education, leadership studies, nonprofit management, community development, organizational leadership, public administration, agriculture, human services, or closely related fields.
* Demonstrated leadership and management skills through collaborations and partnerships with agencies and organizations is necessary.
* Documented experience in volunteer management, organizational development, program coordination, resource development, supervision, and team leadership is desirable.
* Proficiency in oral and written communication and knowledge and use of computer technology for educational programming and management are required.
* Experience working with advisory committees, focus groups, and volunteer organizations is desirable.
* Experience developing and delivering volunteer training programs is desirable.
* Experience working with the media and web-based information delivery methods is desirable.

**Preferred Experience:**

* Successful experience in developing financial support for educational programs through grant writing, fundraising, sponsorship development, contracting, or cost recovery efforts.
* Experience managing budgets, equipment inventories, and program resources.
* Extension or similar outreach education experience.

**Special Requirements:**

* Ability to meet travel demands of position (overnight stays), such as 4-H youth camps, conferences, professional development sessions and training.
* Willingness to work flexible hours, including nights and weekends.
* Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and work outdoors in varying weather conditions.

**Position Assignment:**

* The Service Assistant Professor and/or Service Instructor positions are 12-month, full-time, non-tenure-track faculty positions.
* The successful candidate will be evaluated for providing a significant contribution in service and teaching. Accomplishments will be evaluated at least annually and will be judged in the context of these roles.
* The position will provide statewide leadership for 4-H club development, volunteer management, volunteer compliance, special interest programs, chartering and MOU processes, organizational development, fiscal stewardship, volunteer training, and related youth development initiatives.
* Salary: The fixed salary is $53,000 at the Service Instructor rank and $59,000 at the Service Assistant Professor rank.

**Application Process:**

* Applications will be reviewed beginning immediately and the search will remain open until the position is filled.
* If you meet the stated requirements and would like to be considered for the position, ALL of the following information must be submitted using https://careers.wvu.edu/career-opportunities:
  + Cover letter indicating the position that you are applying for and outlining experience and qualifications.
  + Resume or curriculum vitae including dates of employment, supervisor(s) name and contact information.
  + Three (3) references (including address, e-mail and phone) who can reflect on your professional strengths.
  + Transcripts (undergraduate and/or graduate). Degree must be conferred by start of position.

**About WVU Extension:**

WVU Extension is a primary outreach division of West Virginia University, embracing the heart of the University's land-grant mission. WVU Extension maintains a presence and connections in communities across all 55 West Virginia counties. It assesses local needs, seeks science-based best practices to meet these needs, and delivers educational programs and resources through several formal and informal systems. These connections are critical to the design, implementation, and evaluation of Extension and community engagement programs.

WVU Extension envisions a West Virginia where all its people can reach their fullest potential. Our mission is to improve lives and livelihoods of all West Virginians. Extension’s work is guided by collaboration and partnership; doing no harm; providing trusted, science-based practical education; helping people help themselves; serving all people, and exercising accountability. WVU Extension focuses on providing trusted and practical educational programs that improve health, education, and prosperity. These programs help people, businesses, and communities solve problems, develop skills, and build a better future.

WVU Extension is part of the National Cooperative Extension System present in every state and territory and is overseen by the USDA National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA). It was created by Congress through the 1914 Smith-Lever Act. It is designed as a collaborative program funded through federal, state, and local match. WVU Extension also includes the Fire Service Extension (c. 1931), the Institute for Labor Studies and Research (c. 1959); the Occupational Health and Safety Extension (c. 1988), and the WVU Center for Community Engagement (c. 2021). Visit WVU Extension Service's website at https://extension.wvu.edu/ for additional information about our programs.

**About WVU**

West Virginia University is a place of purpose and community. We take pride in our profound impact on the state of West Virginia and are committed to the personal and professional growth of our employees.

From the groundbreaking R1 research at our flagship campus in Morgantown to the career-oriented programs at WVU Potomac State in Keyser, and the technology-intensive programs at WVU Tech in Beckley, the contributions of WVU employees resonate across the state, touching lives and shaping futures.

At WVU, you will discover a supportive community that champions work-life balance and fosters a collaborative atmosphere. Our core values — service, curiosity, respect, accountability and appreciation — unite us as Mountaineers.

Join us at West Virginia University, where your work will make a lasting impact. To learn more about WVU, visit wvu.edu.

West Virginia University is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We invite all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or Veteran status.

jobs.title: Director of Collection & Resource Services and Assistant/Associate Professor - Odum Library
jobs.description:
**About Us**
------------

  

As a comprehensive institution of the University System of Georgia, Valdosta State University (VSU) is a welcoming, aware, and vibrant community founded on and dedicated to serving our communities' rich and diverse heritages. Through excellence in teaching, basic and applied research, and service, VSU provides rigorous programs and opportunities that enrich our students, our university, and our region. As such, the VSU mission consists of three interrelated parts that includes a student mission, university mission and regional mission. The university is equally dedicated to the core values of community, including a commitment to practice civility, integrity and citizenship. As members of this community and proud Blazers we strive to uphold these core values for the advancement of the University, as stated in the Blazer Creed and reflected in our commitment to the University System of Georgia's Core Values.

**Blazer Creed**

Valdosta State University is a learning environment based on trust and mutual respect in which open dialogue, vigorous debate, and the free exchange of ideas are welcome. The University is equally dedicated to the core values of community, including a commitment to practice **civility, integrity,** and **citizenship.** As members of this community, and proud Blazers, we will strive to uphold these core values for the advancement of the University.

**Civility** - A Blazer shows courtesy and compassion as well as respect for the dignity of every human being.

**Integrity** - Each Blazer is responsible for his or her own actions, and our community is stronger when we contemplate the context of our decisions and uphold the principles of trust and honesty.

**Citizenship** - Every Blazer has an interest in the well-being of the community, and, therefore, a duty to stay informed, to make positive contributions, and to offer support to those who need help.

As a Blazer, we pledge to uphold the core principles of **Civility, Integrity,** and **Citizenship**

**Job Summary**
---------------

  

Odum Library seeks qualified applicants for the Director of Collection and Resource Services, a 12-month tenure track faculty position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor, that begins as early as January 2027. Rank is determined at the time of hiring and will be commensurate with experience. The selected candidate will lead the Collection and Resource Services unit, be responsible for the acquisition and collection development of library collections, maintaining scholarly productivity, and participating in service at the college, university, state and/or national levels.

Review of completed applications will begin October 14, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. For more information on the position, contact Jessica Lee, Electronic Resources & Serials Librarian, via email at jessicalee@valdosta.edu.

**Application Process**

Online application is required. Applicants will be required to attach the following to their online application:

* CV
* Cover Letter
* Unofficial Transcripts (Official Transcripts and Official International Course-by-Course Evaluations Due Upon Hire)
* Names, phone numbers, and email addresses of at least three references

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

  

**Typical Allocation of Duties****:**

25% Accomplish department/unit objectives
  
Direct the human, financial, and other resources needed to accomplish objectives of the department or unit.

20% Monitor and establish processes
  
Monitor and establish processes to ensure effectiveness, efficiency, and alignment with University and department goals.

20% Direct operations
  
Direct the operations of the department or unit.

15% Area Representative
  
Represent the department or unit to internal and external groups and individuals.

10% Manage budget
  
Manage the department/unit budget.

10% Compliance
  
Ensure commitment to and compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and standards

**Supervisor Expectations****:**

**Director of Collection and Resource Services**

* Serve on the library's leadership team.
* Provide leadership and guide the direction for the following areas: acquisitions, collection development, cataloging, electronic resources.
* Supervise two faculty and four staff members.
* Lead initiatives that increase usability and make it easier for students to use resources independently.

**Acquisitions**

* Responsible for purchasing library materials including the acquisition and renewal of electronic database package subscriptions, individual serials, standing orders, books and other library materials.
* Create and update ledgers. Monitor expenditures in the integrated library system (Alma) and VSU fiscal systems and create reports as needed.
* Develop and maintain a positive working relationship with other campus entities including Procurement, Financial Services, and Budget Services.
* Establish and maintain vendor relationships, communicate needs, stay current with new products, product improvements, access and licensing alternatives.

**Collection Development**

* Coordinate collection development including reviewing usage of library resources, recommend adding or removing resources, and ensuring library collection supports curriculum.
* Prepare library portion of accreditation reports and meet with visitation teams.

**Scholarship, Professional Development, and Service**

* Maintain working knowledge of emerging trends in librarianship, acquisitions, and collection development.
* Engage in service at the library, the university, state and/or national level.
* Participate in scholarship, research, and/or creative activity. Contribute to the development of the library profession through scholarship, presentations, and publications.

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

* Master's degree in library and information science from an ALA accredited program.
* Minimum of three years of progressive experience in cataloging, acquisitions, electronic resource management, or a related field in an academic library setting.
* Supervisory experience.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills, organizational skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Familiarity with negotiating licenses and managing e-resources.
* Experience in maintaining effective relationships with vendors and participating in consortia purchasing agreements.
* Strong project management skills and attention to detail.
* Experience with the processes of procurement, contracts, or licensing.

**Proposed Salary**
-------------------

  

Commensurate with experience.

**USG Core Values**
-------------------

  

The University System of Georgia is comprised of our 26 institutions of higher education and learning as well as the System Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. More details on the USG Statement of Core Values and Code of Conduct are available in USG Board Policy 8.2.18.1.2 and can be found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section8/C224/#p8.2.18\_personnel\_conduct.

Additionally, USG supports Freedom of Expression as stated in Board Policy 6.5 Freedom of Expression and Academic Freedom found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section6/C2653.

**Conditions of Employment**
----------------------------

  

Applicants are required to provide:

* professional references with current contact information
* documentation of academic credentials
* employment history

Please note that during the search process, VSU reserves the right to:

* ask candidates who will serve in Positions of Trust to disclose criminal record history during the initial screening process and prior to a conditional offer of employment,
* view social media outlets, and
* remove job postings without additional notification.

Employment is contingent upon:

* successful completion of a background check investigation, including a criminal background check
* reference checks

Employment may also be contingent upon the job-based requirements if applicable for your position:

* satisfactory credit check
* successful completion of a Motor Vehicle Report (MVR)
* pre-employment drug testing
* confirmation of credentials

After initial hiring, employees will be required to successfully complete all of the following training:

  + Drug Free Workplace
  + Sexual Misconduct and Title IX
  + Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)
  + Motor Vehicle Policy

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Valdosta State University is an equal opportunity educational institution. It is not the intent of the institution to discriminate against any applicant for admission, or any student or employee of the institution based on the age, sex, race, religion, color, national origin, disability, or sexual orientation of the individual.

Position of Trust + Credit

If you are a qualified individual with a disability, you may request a reasonable accommodation if you are unable or limited in your ability to access job openings, apply for a job on this site, or participate in the search process as a result of your disability. You can request reasonable accommodations by contacting our Benefits Team, in the Office of Human Resources at vsubenefits@valdosta.edu

**Special Applicant Instructions**
----------------------------------

  

Valdosta State University may provide employment-based immigration sponsorship for select positions when consistent with institutional needs, University policy, and applicable law. Sponsorship is considered on a case-by-case basis and is not available for all positions. Applicants who anticipate requiring employer sponsorship now or in the future are encouraged to contact Human Resources early in the recruitment process with questions regarding sponsorship eligibility.

The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate programs in elementary education, with particular emphasis on literacy, inclusive teaching practices, and curriculum and instruction. We are especially interested in candidates whose teaching, scholarship, and professional engagement reflect current research and evidence-based practices in elementary education and who are committed to meaningful partnerships with schools and communities.
  
  
This position offers opportunities to teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students, supervise candidates in field-based settings, develop a productive program of research and scholarship, collaborate with faculty and school/community partners, and contribute to the ongoing development of innovative educator preparation programs.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* University-level teaching experience (at least one academic semester/3 months).
* Expertise in literacy instruction and knowledge of current research and evidence-based approaches to literacy teaching, including developments associated with the Science of Reading.
* Knowledge of, and experience with, using current approaches to inclusive teaching, culturally responsive and sustaining pedagogies, and/or equitable educational practice while teaching learners with a wide range of strengths, needs, experiences, and backgrounds
* Experience supervising pre-service teachers or other educator candidates in field-based settings.
* Demonstrated commitment to and experience with partnerships involving schools, families, communities, and/or community agencies.
* Record of seeking and/or obtaining external grant funding.
* Experience effectively integrating educational technologies into teaching, including online or technology-enhanced instruction.
* Evidence of effective collaboration with colleagues and other educational partners.

**Position Description & Details**
----------------------------------

  

**Position Summary:**

The History program, part of the Department of Humanities, Social Sciences, and Interdisciplinary Studies at Minot State University, Minot, ND, invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in 20th-century American History to begin in August 2027. The successful candidate should be able to teach general education courses in American history and upper-level courses in areas of specialization. Experience working with and supervising student teachers is highly desirable. Ability to mentor and supervise student applied projects strongly encouraged.

**Requirements:**

The successful candidate will teach four courses each term. Student teacher supervision counts as one of these courses. Most classes are offered on-campus with some potentially offered in a hybrid/remote format. This position emphasizes teaching as well as an ongoing commitment to research and university service. The candidate should have a Ph.D. in History awarded by August 2027.

**Benefits:**

Minot State University offers a competitive benefit package including employer paid full family health insurance, TIAA retirement plan, tuition waiver benefits for employees and their spouses/dependents, and more. Explore MSU Benefits.

**Application Process:**

Submit application materials via MSU’s electronic application system.

A letter of application, curriculum vitae, unofficial graduate transcripts, a statement of teaching philosophy, a summary of research interests, and three references who may be called upon to supply letters of recommendation.

Review of applications will begin October 23, 2026.

**Screening:**

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the US and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. This position does not support visa sponsorship for continued employment.

**About Us**
------------

  

Located in north central North Dakota, Minot State University is a place where east meets west. Nestled on the northern edge of the Mouse River Valley, the campus stands at the heart of the "Magic City." The city of Minot - nicknamed the "Magic City" for its phenomenal growth during the early 1900s - is a regional center for commerce, culture, healthcare, agribusiness and industry.

Minot is home to Minot Air Force Base and is a key service provider in the burgeoning Bakken oil that's made North Dakota's economy one of the strongest in the United States. Minot State University is a public university dedicated to excellence in education, scholarship, and community engagement achieved through rigorous academic experiences, active learning environments, commitment to public service, and a vibrant campus life. Our athletic programs participate in the Northern Sun Intercollegiate Conference in the NCAA Division II.

**Job Description:**
--------------------

The Department of Geography and Anthropology at Louisiana State University invites applications for a tenure-track **Assistant/Associate/Full** **Professor of Human Geography specializing in Geographic Information Science and Technology (GISc&T) and geospatial data science.** We seek a scholar with strong expertise in **GISc&T and advanced geospatial methods** to answer complex societal and human-environment questions.

Relevant methodological expertise may include spatial-temporal analysis, geospatial data science, remote sensing, GeoAI, WebGIS, geovisualization, or related computational approaches. Candidates are not expected to specialize in all these areas. We are particularly interested in candidates who can expand the department's methodological capacity and contribute to innovative applications of geospatial technologies in research and teaching.

The substantive area of specialization is open, but the successful candidate's scholarship must have a strong **human-geographic dimension**. Research areas may include, but are not limited to, health and well-being, population and inequality, food systems, energy and infrastructure, environmental change, hazards and disaster vulnerability, community resilience, critical GIS, or other societally relevant dimensions of human-environment interaction. We welcome scholarship that uses geospatial methods not simply as technical tools, but to advance understanding of important social, spatial, and environmental problems.

The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate instruction in **GISc&T, spatial-temporal analysis, and environmental studies**, while developing courses in their areas of methodological and topical expertise. The position will also offer opportunities to contribute to and collaborate with the department's Environmental Studies and **Disaster Science and Management** areas and to strengthen interdisciplinary geospatial training across departmental programs in both geography and anthropology.

The successful candidate will be expected to develop an externally fundable research program; teach undergraduate and graduate courses; mentor undergraduate, master's, and doctoral students; and contribute to the department's growing emphasis on interdisciplinary and community-engaged scholarship. Opportunities exist for collaboration across geography and anthropology and with programs and units throughout LSU, such as the South Central Climate Adaptation Science Center.

**Job Description:**

50% - Teach graduate or undergraduate courses and hold regular office hours. Supervise graduate assistant(s) if assigned.

50% - Maintain an active research agenda with regular publications.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

Assistant Professor: PhD in Geography or related field or Anticipated Completion of Degree by August of 2027

Associate Professor: PhD in Geography or related field + 6 years of higher education experience

Full Professor: PhD in Geography or related field + 10 years of higher education experience

*Proven record of excellence in teaching and scholarship.*
